name: You Don't Know Jack 2015
description: Fast-paced, irreverent trivia with a snarky host, Dis or Dat rounds, and classic YDKJ absurdist humor. Low player cap — better for small groups.

name: Fibbage XL
description: Fill blanks in weird true facts with convincing lies, then spot the real answer among the fakes. Also available as a standalone purchase.

name: Drawful
description: Draw ridiculous prompts on your phone and everyone tries to guess what it is — then votes on the best wrong answer. The original.

name: Word Spud
description: A word-chain game where players add entries to a growing prompt and the group votes thumbs up or down. Generally considered the weakest game in Pack 1.

name: Lie Swatter
description: True/false trivia buzzer game where up to 100 players participate simultaneously. Jackbox's first mass-participation game — all players play at once, no audience mode needed.

name: Fibbage 2
description: Sequel to Fibbage with more questions and early audience participation — fill blanks in strange true facts with convincing lies.

name: Earwax
description: Pick sound effect combos to answer a prompt, then one rotating judge decides which sounds best fit — like Cards Against Humanity but with audio clips.

name: Bidiots
description: Draw secret items then bid on other players' drawings in an art auction — try to win the items you know about without tipping anyone off.

name: Quiplash XL
description: Write funny answers to prompts and the audience votes on the best one. Expanded version of the original Quiplash with more question content.

name: Bomb Corp.
description: Cooperative bomb-defusal — each player holds different instructions and must communicate fast to cut the right wires before time runs out.

name: Quiplash 2
description: The gold-standard party game. Write funny answers, audience votes, new Thriplash finale. Also available standalone as Quiplash 2 InterLASHional (multilingual).

name: Trivia Murder Party
description: Horror-themed trivia where wrong answers drop you into deadly mini-games. Eliminated players come back as ghosts to haunt the living.

name: Guesspionage
description: Guess what percentage of surveyed people answered a question a certain way, while others bet on whether you're too high or too low.

name: Fakin' It
description: One player secretly doesn't see the prompt and must fake their responses convincingly while everyone tries to identify the faker. Werewolf in quick rounds.

name: Tee K.O.
description: Draw images and write slogans separately — the game mashes them into T-shirt designs that compete in bracket voting. Results are always chaotic and hilarious.

name: Fibbage 3
description: Third Fibbage with a new Enough About You mode where the blanks are facts about your fellow players rather than world trivia.

name: Survive the Internet
description: Answer innocent questions, then other players recontextualize your answers to look absolutely terrible online. A social media pile-on simulator.

name: Monster Seeking Monster
description: A dating-sim social game where players are secretly assigned monster types with hidden powers — send date requests and collect the most hearts to win.

name: Bracketeering
description: Players answer weird questions and vote on which answers win in single-elimination brackets. The highest active player count of any in-pack Jackbox game (16).

name: Civic Doodle
description: Teams build on a shared public drawing in alternating rounds, then the audience votes on which team contributed the best additions to the artwork.

name: You Don't Know Jack: Full Stream
description: YDKJ rebuilt for streaming — a live host reads questions and audience members can actively screw over the main players in real time.

name: Split the Room
description: Twilight Zone-themed game where players complete hypothetical scenarios specifically designed to split the vote exactly 50/50. The closer to the middle, the better.

name: Mad Verse City
description: Giant robot monsters rap-battle using rhymes you write. The game auto-generates a beat and performs your lyrics while the audience votes on the best rapper.

name: Patently Stupid
description: Invent and pitch absurd products to solve ridiculous problems — draw your invention and convince investors (other players + audience) to fund it.

name: Zeeple Dome
description: Fast-paced alien arena combat where you fling your character with a phone touchscreen. More actual video game than party game — the odd one out in Pack 5.

name: Trivia Murder Party 2
description: Sequel with new mini-games, more questions, and the same hotel-horror setting. Dead players still try to haunt their way back to life in the finale.

name: Dictionarium
description: Players define, use in a sentence, and create a synonym for a made-up word across three voting rounds — the funniest answer at each stage wins.

name: Push the Button
description: Aliens secretly control some players and give subtly wrong answers to questions. Humans must investigate and vote to eject suspects before the ship launches.

name: Joke Boat
description: Write punchlines to comedy templates (stand-up Mad Libs), then perform your jokes while the audience votes on the best comedian aboard the cruise ship.

name: Role Models
description: Players categorize each other into pop-culture archetypes (Ninja Turtles, Hogwarts houses, etc.). The most agreed-upon and funniest placements score points.

name: Quiplash 3
description: Third Quiplash with the new Thriplash final round where three players compete on one prompt. Audience votes count throughout every round.

name: The Devils and the Details
description: Play a family of devils blending into suburban life by completing mundane tasks — but secretly some players are selfish and will sabotage the team score.

name: Champ'd Up
description: Draw original champions to represent absurd categories, then your creations face off in head-to-head bracket battles voted on by everyone.

name: Talking Points
description: Improvise a speech while random slides you've never seen appear behind you. Others guess what the speech is supposed to be about. Improv comedy gold.

name: Blather 'Round
description: Describe a secret thing using only sentence-fragment clues from a limited word bank — first to guess correctly scores, and guessers can interrupt at any time.

name: Drawful Animate
description: Evolved Drawful where players draw two-frame animations instead of static images. Supports custom episode creation with your own prompts.

name: Job Job
description: Answer questions, then answer new questions using only words from other players' previous answers. The constraints create beautifully chaotic results.

name: Wheel of Enormous Proportions
description: Trivia game where correct answers earn wheel slices. The more you answer correctly, the more chances your name lands on the spinning prize wheel.

name: Weapons Drawn
description: You're secretly both a murderer and a detective. Hide a letter of your name in your murder weapon drawing while hunting for hidden letters in others'.

name: The Poll Mine
description: Teams answer survey questions then must rank the results in correct order to escape a dungeon. Cooperative survey guessing with team-vs-team split.

name: Fibbage 4
description: Fourth Fibbage with new modes: Enough About You (personal facts) and Short Fuse (timed fast-paced variant) alongside the classic format.

name: Nonsensory
description: Draw or write a response to a prompt placed on an absurd scale — then everyone guesses exactly where on the scale each player positioned their answer.

name: Roomerang
description: Reality TV competition parody — answer questions, compete in challenges, and vote each other off one by one until the last player standing wins.

name: Junktopia
description: You've been transformed into an object. Write creative backstories for random junk items to maximize their auction appraisal — highest value wins.

name: Quixort
description: Trivia sorting conveyor belt — players or teams arrange falling answers in the correct order before they pile up. Works great for two big teams.

name: Tee K.O. 2
description: Sequel to the fan-favorite T-shirt game with new mechanics. Draw images, write slogans, the game combines them into shirts that compete in bracket voting.

name: Timejinx
description: Timeline-based trivia — guess the year events happened. Accuracy counts more than pure recall; close guesses still score, and a wrong guess can jinx others.

name: FixyText
description: Receive garbled autocorrect messages and fill in the most hilarious plausible interpretation of what was being texted. Fast and funny.

name: Dodo Re Mi
description: Assign notes to cute animal characters and collaborate to perform a song. Audience members can join in on extra instruments — unique musical chaos.

name: Hypnotorious
description: Everyone's been hypnotized into secretly liking something absurd. Ask questions to figure out others' obsessions while hiding your own.

name: Doominate
description: Head-to-head joke writing — compete to write the most devastating way to ruin a perfectly lovely situation, with audience voting on the winner.

name: Hear Say
description: Record sound effects and voice clips on your phone — the game stitches them into short movie scenes and others guess what's happening from the audio alone.

name: Cookie Haus
description: Design and name cookies to fulfill orders from eccentric clients. The audience votes on which designs best meet each unusual brief.

name: Suspectives
description: One player secretly committed the crime and must defend their innocence using survey-sourced evidence while others investigate and try to name the culprit.

name: Legends of Trivia
description: Team-based trivia in a fantasy RPG world — assemble your party and face off in knowledge battles with RPG-style stakes and progression.

name: Dirty Drawful
description: The adult version of Drawful with explicit prompts and player-submitted content. No family-friendly mode — the whole game is adult by design.

name: Fakin' It All Night Long
description: Adult version of Fakin' It with mature prompts and an adjustable intensity slider. One player still doesn't see the prompt and must fake their responses.

name: Let Me Finish
description: A debate game with absurd adult hypotheticals. Players argue for their answers in a structured format with an intensity slider for content level.

name: Quiplash
description: The original standalone Quiplash — write funny answers to prompts and the audience votes. The game that popularized the format before the party packs.

name: Drawful 2
description: Standalone sequel to the original Drawful with custom episode support — create your own prompt packs. Frequently goes on deep sale.

name: Quiplash 2 InterLASHional
description: Standalone multilingual version of Quiplash 2 (EN/FR/DE/IT/ES) for international groups. Same fill-in-the-blank format with audience voting and Thriplash finale.

name: The Jackbox Survey Scramble
description: Six survey mini-games in one standalone package with an evolving dataset built from real player answers. Supports up to 10 players — great for larger groups.

name: Gartic Phone
description: Free browser game combining Telephone and Pictionary — players alternate drawing and writing captions, producing hilariously broken chains. Best at 6–12. No download required.

name: skribbl.io
description: Free browser Pictionary — one player draws while others race to guess the word. Private rooms support up to 20 with custom word lists. No download required.

name: Codenames Online
description: Free browser version of the hit board game. Two spymasters give one-word clues to lead their teams to the right code words while avoiding the assassin card.

name: Among Us
description: The iconic social deduction game — crewmates complete tasks while impostors secretly sabotage and eliminate them. Free on mobile, paid on PC.

name: Kahoot!
description: Quiz platform where the host creates questions and players answer on their phones. Free tier supports up to 10 players; paid plans scale to 2,000+.
